correctness.rationale: For every target, singleton discrepancy limits predecessor-set size to two. Equality at 2n forces all rows two-element. Pair discrepancy makes rows pairwise intersecting, implying star or triangle. For n>=5 the full-set image must have n-1 elements, excluding triangles. Star rows {c,f(y)} satisfy the all-subset bound precisely when f(W) has at least n-2 distinct outputs. Surjections and Stirling identities count n!(C(n,2)+C(n,3)+3C(n,4)) labelled cases. At n=4 all three triangle edges must occur, yielding 4*3!S(4,3)=144 additional cases and 312 stars. Checker independently exhausts all relations n<=4 and 2-regular columns n=4,5; code does not replace general proof.
